solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Untimely error upsets a Cornishman

indicators.note: to upset something is to knock it over and disorder it, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man from Cornwall is knocked over by a mistake about the date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsets' rearranges the eleven letters of A CORNISHMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of its proper period, like a clock in a Roman play, is a chronological mistake.

clue.text: He was inundated with entries from couples

definitions.text: He was inundated with entries from couples

parts.words: He was inundated with entries from couples
parts.note: reads like someone swamped with applications from pairs; really the biblical ark-builder who took animals aboard two by two before the Flood

explanation.surface: A man overwhelmed by submissions from pairs of people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Genesis patriarch admitted the animals in pairs to his ark, and the waters then flooded the earth.

clue.text: See the N American Indian creep softly away

indicators.note: away means the letter for softly is taken off and removed from the word creep

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: Watch the Native American sneak off quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See the' is just a link; 'creep softly away' is CREEP with P (piano, soft in music) gone.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a First Nations people of Canada and the northern United States.

clue.text: Uncommon payment for an author

explanation.surface: An unusual fee for a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncommon' looks like an adjective meaning rare; it stands for those of noble birth, the opposite of commoners.
explanation.definitionFit: Kings and princes are not commoners, so 'uncommon' people; and a writer earns a percentage per copy sold.

clue.text: Steer straight

explanation.surface: Drive directly ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steer' looks like a verb about driving; it is the young bullock.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for cattle or an ox, and also the term for spirits served undiluted, without water or ice.

clue.text: Notices damaged part

indicators.note: something damaged is broken out of shape, so the letters of notices are rearranged

explanation.surface: Signs that have been vandalised in places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges the letters of NOTICES.
explanation.definitionFit: A division or portion of a whole, as in a section of a book or orchestra.

clue.text: Resistance leader who aimed to avert a family tragedy

definitions.text: Resistance leader who aimed to avert a family tragedy

parts.words: Resistance leader who aimed to avert a family tragedy
parts.note: the Swiss folk hero who led resistance to Austrian rule, forced to shoot an apple off his son's head; his careful aim avoided killing the boy

explanation.surface: A rebel chief took care not to cause a domestic disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Swiss crossbowman shot an apple from his son's head and became a symbol of resistance to Habsburg rule.

clue.text: Show how devil and saint rank in estimation

parts.note: a devil is a demon
to rate something is to rank it in estimation

explanation.surface: Explain how a fiend and a holy person compare in people's opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: To show how something works by example is to give a practical display of it.

clue.text: High flier subject to ground control

definitions.text: High flier subject to ground control

parts.words: High flier subject to ground control
parts.note: suggests an aircraft guided by air-traffic controllers; really a toy flown on a string held by someone on the ground

explanation.surface: An aircraft steered by controllers on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper or fabric toy flies high in the wind while held on a string from the ground.

clue.text: One won't strike unless the conditions are right

definitions.text: One won't strike unless the conditions are right

parts.words: One won't strike unless the conditions are right
parts.note: reads like a cautious trade unionist; really a match that lights only when rubbed on the special strip on its box

explanation.surface: A worker who will only walk out if the circumstances suit.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of match ignites only when struck on the prepared surface of its box, unlike a strike-anywhere match.

clue.text: Further chaos in Laos

indicators.note: chaos is disorder, so the letters of Laos are jumbled

explanation.surface: More turmoil in the Southeast Asian country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaos' signals a rearrangement of LAOS; 'in' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean in addition or besides, as in 'further, it was raining'.

clue.text: They follow, one falls but the other breaks

definitions.text: They follow, one falls but the other breaks

parts.words: They follow, one falls but the other breaks
parts.note: a pair that succeed each other endlessly; darkness is said to fall and dawn to break

explanation.surface: Two things in sequence: one drops and the other shatters.
explanation.definitionFit: The two halves of the daily cycle follow each other, and we say darkness falls while dawn breaks.

clue.text: Suitable way to obtain without payment

explanation.surface: A proper method for getting something for free.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is an adjective in one sense and a verb in the other, pronounced differently; 'way to' just links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means fitting; as a verb it means to take for one's own use without permission or paying.

clue.text: Irreverence shown by cheeky child I have yet to reform

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so the letters of yet are rearranged

explanation.surface: Disrespect from a naughty youngster who has still not mended their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reform' rearranges YET into ETY; 'shown by' and 'have' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of reverence or piety, especially towards God, is disrespect.

clue.text: Indeed a way used to get a rise

parts.note: ye is an old form of yea, meaning yes or indeed
ST, short for street, is a way

explanation.surface: Indeed, one route employed to win promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: This fungus is added to dough so that it ferments and rises.

clue.text: Scope for firm with a thousand to spend

parts.note: CO, short for company, is a firm
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
to pass time is to spend it

explanation.surface: Room for a business with a thousand pounds to pay out.
explanation.definitionFit: Range or extent, as in 'within the compass of the law'.

clue.text: A fisherman will use many a spinner

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
a reel spins as the line is wound

explanation.surface: An angler will need lots of lures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinner' suggests the fishing lure; here it is the reel on the rod, which turns.
explanation.definitionFit: This wicker basket is what an angler keeps the catch in.

clue.text: Long story set about drug

indicators.note: the story is set about, surrounding the drug

parts.note: a yarn is a story
E is short for ecstasy, a drug

explanation.surface: A lengthy tale about a narcotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective; it is the verb, to long for.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to desire it intensely.

clue.text: Quite a lot of transferable stock?

definitions.text: Quite a lot of transferable stock?

parts.words: Quite a lot of transferable stock?
parts.note: suggests a sizeable parcel of shares in the financial sense; really livestock, a group of cattle moved together

explanation.surface: A large holding of shares that can be traded.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of cattle is livestock that can be driven from place to place.

clue.text: Starts to serve time in Russian prison

indicators.note: the starts of these four words, their initial letters, are taken

explanation.surface: Beginning a sentence in a Russian jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts to' takes the first letters of 'serve time in Russian'. STIR is old slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: This is old slang for a jail, as in 'doing time in the stir'.

clue.text: He goes into a ship and remains

indicators.note: goes into means one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man boards a vessel and stays put.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remains' looks like a verb; it is the noun, what is left after burning.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left after a cremation or fire is the powdery residue.

clue.text: Hospital worker once left doctor in near chaos

indicators.note: in means L and MO sit inside the jumbled letters
chaos is disorder, so the letters of near are jumbled

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A former hospital employee left a doctor in near turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of the fodder gives ANER, opened up by the container. 'once' marks the definition as dated: the job title is no longer used in British hospitals.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the former title of a hospital social worker in Britain, who looked after patients' welfare.

clue.text: Pays one's bills and relaxes

explanation.surface: Clears what is owed and takes it easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is just a link between the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear what is owed is to pay up; it also means to calm down and get comfortable.

clue.text: Stop when confronted by snake on the road

indicators.note: the stop is faced by the snake, which stands before it

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
to halt is to stop

explanation.surface: Pull up when a snake appears in front of you on the highway.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the surfacing material found on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: This tarry black material is what most roads are surfaced with.

clue.text: Tract of grassland left untidy

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or grassland

indicators.note: untidy means messed about, so the letters of left are rearranged

explanation.surface: An area of meadow left unkempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tract' looks like a stretch of land; it is the printed pamphlet. 'untidy' rearranges LEFT into FLET.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a short pamphlet, usually on a religious or political subject.

clue.text: The prosecutor is on the platform

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, a US public prosecutor

explanation.surface: The lawyer takes the stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised stage at one end of a hall, where speakers sit.

clue.text: Hare bumped into ostrich

indicators.note: something bumped is knocked about, so the letters of hare are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hare collided with a big flightless bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bumped' rearranges HARE; 'into' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is the South American ostrich, a large flightless bird of the same family.

clue.text: Flag raised around site of the Taj Mahal

indicators.note: the flag raised is wrapped around the answer, which sits in the middle

explanation.surface: A banner is hoisted near the famous Indian monument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' tempts a reversal; it is only part of the cover, with 'around' showing the answer inside 'Flag raised'.
explanation.definitionFit: The city in Uttar Pradesh, India, is where the famous white marble mausoleum stands.

clue.text: When it falls, it has the cheek to go on

definitions.text: When it falls, it has the cheek to go on

parts.words: When it falls, it has the cheek to go on
parts.note: sounds like something impudent; really a drop from the eye that rolls down the face

explanation.surface: Something so brazen that it carries on when it drops.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop of salty fluid from the eye runs down the face when someone cries.

clue.text: Theologians may provide choice literary gatherings

indicators.note: the letters of theologians can be reworked to provide the answer

explanation.surface: Religious scholars could supply collections of fine writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may provide' signals rearranging the letters of THEOLOGIANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Collections of selected poems or writings are gathered together in one volume.

clue.text: Drink, knock it back as a starter

indicators.note: as a starter means the word as comes first
back means the word it is read backwards

explanation.surface: Down the wine as an aperitif.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock' is part of the cover, making 'knock it back' sound like drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: This sparkling white wine comes from the Piedmont region of Italy.

clue.text: Kent resort offers wide-ranging flights

parts.note: broad means wide-ranging
flights of stairs

explanation.surface: A seaside town offers broad staircases.
explanation.walkthrough: BROADSTAIRS is a seaside town on the Kent coast in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a seaside town on the Isle of Thanet in Kent, south-east England.
